investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for 131–146 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never produced a running VM, so none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were written, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) was fully violated. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for 131–146 seconds before the eval timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never produced a running VM, so none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were written, and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) was fully violated. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or invoking the runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule a new agent pod. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 match the pod's node affinity/selector for remote agents, and both of those nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM resource quota on those nodes is fully consumed. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. The pod remained Unschedulable for 131–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code failure, and it is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; this is an eval-level detection of a resource exhaustion condition.
